mechanism_narrative: The continued decline in WORKPLACES mobility signals a slower commuting economy, but the concurrent easing of that decline implies people are reallocating time toward discretionary shopping trips. If WORKPLACES stops falling, RETAIL_REC should rise over the next four weeks as weekday non-work errands expand.
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES improved from -28.6 to -19.6 while RETAIL_REC improved from -15.7 to -10.7
failure_condition: If WORKPLACES continues to improve but RETAIL_REC remains flat or falls over the next 28 days, this trend mechanism is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A further drop in RESIDENTIAL mobility below the recent 6.9-7.9 range would indicate households are spending less time at home and more time out for discretionary activity. That shift should lift RETAIL_REC within one to two weeks through higher local spending trips.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL falls below 6.5 after being at or above 6.9 in the prior week
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL declined from 9.6 to 6.9 while RETAIL_REC improved from -15.7 to -10.7
failure_condition: If RESIDENTIAL drops below the trigger and RETAIL_REC does not increase within 14 days, the mechanism is false.

mechanism_narrative: When TRANSIT remains deeply depressed but WORKPLACES continues to recover, trips are more likely to shift from commuting into local car-based and nearby retail trips. Under that mixed-access pattern, RETAIL_REC should rise over the next four weeks despite weak transit use.
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT stayed near -46 while WORKPLACES improved from -28.6 to -19.6
failure_condition: If TRANSIT remains below -40 and WORKPLACES keeps improving, but RETAIL_REC does not exceed its last-four-week average, the interaction is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rebound in PARKS mobility above its recent negative levels indicates reopening or looser public-space rules that spill over into discretionary shopping. Once PARKS crosses back into positive territory, RETAIL_REC should improve within two weeks as outing propensity broadens beyond parks.
candidate_trigger: PARKS rises above 0 after being negative for at least two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS fell from -9.4 to -18.0 while RETAIL_REC improved modestly
failure_condition: If PARKS crosses above zero and RETAIL_REC does not rise within 14 days, the spillover hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: Stable or rising GROCERY_PHARM combined with falling RESIDENTIAL means more out-of-home errand chains are being completed during the week. That routine should translate into incremental RETAIL_REC gains over a four-week window because retail trips are bundled with essential trips.
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM stayed around 7.3-7.4 while RESIDENTIAL eased from 9.6 to 6.9
failure_condition: If grocery/pharmacy stays elevated and residential falls but RETAIL_REC does not improve relative to the prior 28 days, the bundling mechanism is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained week-over-week improvement in PARKS from a very negative level often reflects weather normalization rather than policy change, and that same weather effect boosts shopping traffic. If PARKS rebounds by at least five points from its trough, RETAIL_REC should rise in the following week.
candidate_trigger: PARKS increases by at least 5 points from the prior week's value
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS moved from -6.6 to -18.0 over the snapshot while RETAIL_REC improved to -10.7
failure_condition: If PARKS rebounds by 5 points or more and RETAIL_REC does not rise in the next week, the seasonal spillover is false.

mechanism_narrative: In a tightening-restrictions regime, a simultaneous drop in TRANSIT and WORKPLACES should suppress discretionary shopping with a short lag. Because both mobility channels are still far below baseline, any renewed tightening should push RETAIL_REC lower over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT falls below -50 or WORKPLACES falls below -25 after a one-week improvement
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT remained near -46 and WORKPLACES remained below -19.6
failure_condition: If transit and workplaces deteriorate further under tightening conditions but RETAIL_REC does not fall below its recent 28-day average, the hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: The recent simultaneous improvement in WORKPLACES and modest stabilization in GROCERY_PHARM indicates more routine weekday movement, which should keep discretionary retail recovery going. Over the next two weeks, RETAIL_REC should continue moving upward as these everyday trips normalize.
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES improved steadily from -28.6 to -19.6 while GROCERY_PHARM held near 7.3-7.4
failure_condition: If WORKPLACES keeps improving and grocery/pharmacy remains stable, but RETAIL_REC does not rise over the next 14 days, the mechanism is rejected.
